title: WORKING DRAFT — PRD: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools (Console + Control Plane)
content:
Doc status: working draft / pre-Confluence. Expect rough edges. Goal is to align on scope for beta + what is “must ship” vs “nice to have.”

Owner: Marissa (Console & rollouts)
PM partners: Paula (policies/gates), Lauren (Dedicated requirements)
Eng partners (initial): Ethan (control plane), Mina (routing), Chloe/Dylan (console backend), Logan (telemetry), Sean (SRE)

---

1) Summary / tl;dr
Dedicated customers run on reserved GPU pools with strict SLA expectations and little tolerance for “oops deploy.” Today, Dedicated model/runtime/config updates are effectively pool-wide all-at-once (or rely on manual traffic shifting playbooks). A bad change saturates the pool, queue depth explodes, p95/p99 goes red, and we violate latency/availability commitments.

We need first-class staged rollouts for Dedicated pools: define stages (shadow/5%/25%/100%), evaluate gates (latency, errors, queue depth, utilization, etc), require approvals, and pause/rollback safely and audibly.

This PRD is specifically “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools” and is NOT full experimentation/bandits. A/B testing can share the primitives later but is separate.

---

2) Problem statement
Dedicated tenants have:
- fixed capacity (reserved GPU pools) where any regression shows up as immediate queuing
- strict isolation requirements (no cross-tenant interactions)
- contract/SOC2-style change management expectations (approvals + audit trail)

Today’s state (pain):
- “Pool-level flip” model or runtime/config change from vN to vN+1
- Some customers run their own external traffic splitting; many do not
- Redwood oncall ends up firefighting: manual revert, manual routing overrides, unclear “what changed?” timeline

Why now:
- Dedicated adoption is increasing and deals require safer rollouts
- We’ve already seen Dedicated incidents/dogfood near-misses when changes hit full pools
- SRE wants guardrails + stop-the-line behavior (and auditable controls)

---

3) Who is this for (personas)
Primary (v1):
1) Redwood operator (SRE / platform operator) deploying changes to Dedicated pools
2) Enterprise “tenant operator” (customer admin) — limited beta/opt-in only

Secondary:
- Support/CS: visibility into what’s happening + what to tell the customer
- Security/compliance: approvals + audit export

Non-user but impacted:
- Routing / control plane teams (deterministic allocation)
- Fleet/autoscaling teams (headroom policies)

---

4) Goals / non-goals
Goals (v1):
- Multi-stage rollout definition per Dedicated pool
- Deterministic traffic allocation per stage weight, enforced by routing
- Per-stage gates: evaluate over windows; stop/pause on gate failure; optionally auto-rollback depending on policy
- Manual approvals for stage advancement (configurable)
- Audit trail for actions and evaluation results (who/what/when)
- Fail-safe: if metrics missing or evaluator degraded, DO NOT auto-advance

Non-goals (v1):
- Multi-armed bandit / dynamic optimization
- Per-request semantic quality gating for every workload (optional for select customers only)
- Full self-serve rollout management for all Dedicated customers (we’ll start with Redwood operators; enterprise opt-in)

---

5) Customer pain: quotes from CS / Support (raw)
(Collected by Rachel Kim + Miguel Santos; names/company details paraphrased.)

Quote 1 (Enterprise Dedicated, compliance-heavy):
- “We can’t take a pool-wide cutover during business hours. If it goes wrong, we can’t just ‘wait it out’ — it breaches our own SLA to our customers.”

Quote 2 (Mid-market Dedicated):
- “We want to do 5% then 25% then 100% but we don’t have a safe way to do it with the reserved pool. When we tried, latency went up and we didn’t know if it was the new model or capacity.”

Quote 3 (Security review, procurement stage):
- “Who approved the change? Where is the audit trail? Can we export it? If you can’t show approvals and rollback capability, we can’t pass change management controls.”

Quote 4 (Support escalation after incident):
- “Traffic split behavior during a model update felt unpredictable. We tried to ‘slow roll’ but saw bursts of errors. We need something deterministic and observable.”

Quote 5 (CS on what “good” looks like):
- “Even if customers can’t self-serve immediately, we need a clear operational story: staged rollout, pre-defined gates, and a pause/rollback mechanism with comms.”

---

6) Proposed solution (high level)
Introduce a Dedicated rollout plan associated with a pool.
- A rollout plan has stages (ordered) + per-stage weights + gates + approval policy
- The routing layer enforces traffic allocation based on stage weights
- A gate evaluator periodically checks metrics for the stage’s candidate (and/or overall pool health) over an evaluation window
- If gates pass and approval is satisfied, rollout advances to next stage
- If gates fail or metrics are missing/stale, rollout pauses (hold). Optional rollback policy for severe failures.

UX: Console provides
- Create/edit rollout plan via wizard
- Stage detail view with gate pass/fail + last evaluation time + which metric tripped
- Approve / abort / rollback actions
- Audit log view for all rollout events

---

7) Brainstorm: stage types & standard templates
Templates operators can pick from (initial thoughts):
A) Standard staged rollout
- Stage 0: Internal shadow / canary (0% external, 100% shadow?)
- Stage 1: 5%
- Stage 2: 25%
- Stage 3: 100%

B) Conservative rollout (for high-sensitivity tenants)
- Stage 0: shadow
- Stage 1: 1%
- Stage 2: 5%
- Stage 3: 10%
- Stage 4: 25%
- Stage 5: 50%
- Stage 6: 100%

C) Emergency rollout (hotfix)
- Stage 1: 25% (short window)
- Stage 2: 100%

Open question: Do we allow “shadow stage” for Dedicated in v1? Shadow means we run the candidate model for copies of requests but don’t return output; capacity implications are non-trivial.

---

8) Brainstorm: gate types (raw list)
Hard requirement gates for beta (my proposal):
- Availability / error rate gate:
  - 5xx rate (or error_code class) for candidate
  - Timeout rate (client timeouts + server timeouts)
- Latency gate:
  - p95 latency for candidate route/model
  - optionally p99 if stable enough
- Queue depth gate:
  - queue depth threshold (absolute OR delta from baseline)
- Saturation/utilization gate:
  - GPU utilization or “pool saturation” proxy

Nice-to-have gates (beta+ or GA):
- Token throughput regression (tokens/sec) compared to baseline stage
- OOM / eviction rate (KV cache thrash)
- Retry rate (if present in telemetry)
- Cost gate (tokens/$) — likely too noisy initially
- Quality gate (eval set pass rate, or customer-provided reference prompts) — only if available

Meta-gates / safety gates:
- Metrics freshness gate (if metrics lag > X, hold)
- Evaluator health gate (if evaluator degraded, hold all)

Important: Dedicated pools must fail safe. Missing metrics should PAUSE, not “assume pass.”

---

9) Initial default thresholds (VERY ROUGH; needs SRE sign-off)
Note: defaults must be configurable per tenant/pool. We should ship recommended defaults + allow overrides.

Defaults idea (per stage evaluation window: 10–15 minutes; can be longer for low QPS tenants):
- p95 latency: <= baseline_stage_p95 * 1.10 AND <= absolute cap (e.g., 1.5s) (cap depends on customer SLO)
- 5xx rate: <= 0.5% (or <= baseline + 0.2%)
- timeout rate: <= 0.2% (or <= baseline + 0.1%)
- queue depth: <= 2x baseline OR <= absolute threshold (TBD)
- utilization: <= 90% sustained (or more nuanced headroom rule)

Open question: baseline definition. For stage N, do we compare to stage N-1 (current “control”) or to last known good 100%? How do we handle seasonal load changes?

---

10) UX principles (draft)
- Make “what is happening right now” obvious: stage, weight, health, time-in-stage
- Show why we are paused: which gate, which metric, last datapoint, freshness
- Avoid ambiguous states (operators hate “pending??”)— use explicit statuses
- Safe by default: manual approvals on by default for Dedicated
- Provide an escape hatch: abort/rollback action always available to authorized users

---

11) Workflow: operator story (end-to-end)
1) Operator creates a rollout plan for pool P, selecting the change target (model version/runtime/config bundle)
2) Console shows wizard:
   - select pool
   - select change payload
   - choose template (stages)
   - configure gates (defaults pre-filled)
   - choose approval policy (manual each stage vs auto-advance)
3) Rollout starts in stage 1 (or stage 0 shadow if supported)
4) Gate evaluator runs every N minutes; stage shows PASS/FAIL/PENDING due to missing metrics
5) If gates pass, stage becomes “Ready for approval” (or auto-advances)
6) On approval, routing weight changes deterministically; we record an approval event
7) If any gate fails, rollout is paused (hold), routing weight stops progressing, and operator decides to continue, adjust gates, or rollback

Open question: Do we support “edit gates mid-rollout” in beta? If yes, we need robust versioning + audit events.

---

12) Required Console screens (beta)
- Dedicated pool → Rollouts tab: list of rollout plans (active + recent)
- Create staged rollout plan (wizard)
- Rollout plan detail page:
  - stage list with weights, status, time-in-stage
  - gate summary (pass/fail/pending)
  - actions: Approve next stage, Hold, Abort, Rollback
- Gate detail drawer:
  - threshold, current value, evaluation window, query link to dashboard
- Audit log view:
  - filter by actor, action, time range

---

13) Key requirements / acceptance criteria (beta)
Routing + determinism
- Deterministic request-to-variant allocation within stage weight (avoid per-request flapping)
- Tenant isolation preserved (no cross-tenant traffic mixing)
- Clear behavior at 0% and 100% transitions

Gates
- Evaluator supports fixed time windows
- Missing/late metrics cause HOLD
- Evaluator failure causes HOLD globally (or at least blocks auto-advance)

Approvals + audit
- Approval events are stored and visible
- Actor identity + role captured (internal operator vs tenant admin)
- Audit export pipeline compatibility (fields stable)

Safety
- Autoscaling/headroom guardrails considered (esp. when candidate is slower)
- Rollouts cannot progress if pool is already saturated (optional “precheck gate”)

---

14) Out of scope / explicitly deferred decisions
- True shadow traffic for all Dedicated pools (capacity costs)
- Automated rollback policy beyond simple triggers (we can start with “pause only” default)
- Sophisticated baseline comparisons / anomaly detection
- Fully customer-configurable gate query language (we should avoid letting users write PromQL in the UI)

---

15) Risks / concerns (raw)
- Metrics lie / missing data: biggest operational risk. We must hold safely and surface freshness.
- Cardinality explosions if we tag metrics per rollout/stage incorrectly.
- Slow ramp can still saturate reserved pools if candidate throughput regresses; need autoscaling guardrails OR “min headroom” rule.
- Confusing mental model: “stage weight” vs “pool capacity” vs “autoscaling” needs crisp docs.

---

16) Open questions (needs resolution before Confluence PRD)
Product / UX
1) Shadow stage: do we include Stage 0 in beta? If yes, how do we prevent doubling load?
2) Who can create/edit rollout plans during beta (operators only? enterprise opt-in?)
3) Do we allow editing stages/gates while rollout is active? Or require abort + create new plan?
4) What does “Abort” mean vs “Rollback”? (Abort could freeze and leave traffic where it is; rollback actively returns to last stable)

Technical
5) Baseline comparison: stage-to-stage vs last stable 100%? how to compute baseline for low QPS tenants?
6) Evaluation windows: do we gate on “N consecutive passes” to reduce flakiness?
7) Routing behavior under constrained pool: should we reduce candidate weight automatically if queue depth high?
8) What is the source of truth for rollout state: control plane vs console backend cache?

Security / compliance
9) Audit retention: how long do we store events? Are we aligning with existing audit log SLAs?
10) RBAC model: what are minimal roles? (approve vs abort vs edit)

Operational
11) Default policy on gate failure: pause only vs auto-rollback? (SRE preference is often pause; CS preference might be rollback for severe)
12) Alerting: when do we page on paused rollouts vs silent hold? (likely page if stuck > X mins at >Y% stage)

---

17) Proposed success metrics
Beta success
- 0 Sev-1 incidents caused by staged rollout mechanism itself (state machine/routing)
- Detect regressions earlier: >80% of bad changes caught at <=25% stage (proxy: gate failure before 100%)
- Median time to pause on gate failure < 5 minutes after threshold breach (depends on evaluator tick)
- Operator satisfaction: “I can tell what’s happening and why it paused” (qualitative)

GA success
- Adoption: % of Dedicated updates using staged rollouts by default
- Reduced support tickets related to Dedicated update confusion
- Improved SLA adherence during updates

---

18) Notes / next steps
- Align with Sean (SRE) + Allison (observability) on default thresholds + evaluation windows
- Confirm with Ethan/Mina on control plane object model + routing enforcement
- Confirm with Marcus (security) on audit schema and RBAC roles
- After alignment, publish cleaned PRD to Confluence and link from PM-418

TODOs (Marissa)
- Draft user flows for create/edit + approve/abort
- Decide beta scope: operator-only vs enterprise opt-in
- Convert gate brainstorm into crisp “Required for beta” list

End of working draft.
